This section defines the governance controls that shall be applied to manage milestone execution, delivery risk, deferred decisions, and scope integrity across the approved phases of this SOW. It should be read together with Section 9 (Key Deliverables), Section 11 (Acceptance Criteria), Section 13 (Commercials), and Section 17 (Change Management Process). The purpose of this section is to ensure that delivery progression, milestone recognition, and risk treatment remain aligned to approved scope, objective acceptance, and formal governance decisions rather than informal assumptions or downstream execution momentum.

The engagement shall be governed through a milestone-driven delivery structure spanning Explore, Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, and the applicable Hypercare and transition activities for each approved release. For each milestone, completion shall depend on delivery of the relevant approved outputs, satisfaction of the corresponding acceptance criteria, and written confirmation by the designated Google approvers identified elsewhere in this SOW. No milestone shall be interpreted as complete solely because underlying activity has started, internal progress has been reported, or partial outputs exist.

Milestone governance for this engagement shall operate on the following principles:

- Each major phase or release shall have a clearly defined baseline of deliverables, dependencies, assumptions, and sign-off expectations before execution proceeds.
- Milestone progression shall be based on objective evidence of completion, including approved documentation, completed reviews, executed tests, readiness checks, and written approvals where required.
- Milestone recognition shall remain aligned to the agreed deliverables and acceptance framework, and shall not be driven only by elapsed time or internal sprint activity.
- Any unresolved decision, dependency, or assumption that may materially affect scope, design, interfaces, testing, deployment, effort, or commercials shall be logged, assigned an owner, tracked to closure, and escalated through the agreed governance forums.
- Any change affecting milestone scope, deliverables, timing, or commercial impact shall be governed through the Change Management Process in Section 17 before the affected work is treated as committed scope.

For operational clarity, the milestone structure currently intended for this SOW is as follows:

- **Explore milestone** — establishment of the delivery baseline through project planning, governance setup, workshop planning, risk identification, current-state validation, and target-state process and solution definition.
- **Phase 1 milestone** — completion of the foundational design and readiness baseline required to authorize approved realization work across process, application, integration, data, traceability, and planning scope.
- **Realization and testing milestone(s)** — completion of approved build, configuration, technical realization, test preparation, unit testing, system integration testing, user acceptance preparation, training preparation, and related readiness outputs for the approved release baseline.
- **Deployment milestone** — completion of cutover readiness, release controls, production deployment, and production validation for the approved release scope.
- **Hypercare and transition milestone** — completion of agreed post-go-live stabilization, issue disposition, knowledge transfer, transition readiness, and release closure activities.

The milestone-level deliverable structure for this SOW shall follow the approved deliverables already defined elsewhere in this document. At a minimum, the parties acknowledge that milestone execution is expected to rely on deliverables such as the Project Plan, Governance Plan, Workshop Schedule, Risk Assessment & Mitigation Plan, Approved Business Process Document, Finalized RICEFW List, Functional Specifications / User Stories, Data Migration Strategy & Plan, Integration Design Document, Sprint Plan with User Stories, Configuration Design Document, Technical Specifications, playback and feedback outputs, Test Scripts, Training Documents, Unit Test and SIT Results, UAT Results, Train-the-Trainer materials, Cutover Plan, Go-Live and Cutover Checklist, Production Cutover Results, Hypercare Support and Transition Plan, Knowledge Transfer Sign-off, Project Closure Document, Lessons Learned, Issue Tracker, Post-Go-Live Survey, and Status Reports.

The Explore milestone shall serve as the design-baselining and mobilization control point for the engagement. This milestone is intended to confirm that the approved scope has been translated into a governed delivery baseline, that current-state findings and target-state design assumptions have been documented, and that key open decisions affecting later build and deployment are visible and actively managed. Completion of Explore shall not by itself authorize unlimited downstream realization; rather, it shall confirm that the approved next-phase baseline is sufficiently defined to proceed subject to any documented conditions.

The Phase 1 milestone shall serve as the foundational readiness gate for the approved design baseline. This milestone is intended to freeze the approved process, application, integration, data, and technical design direction needed for realization of the committed scope. If any open item at this stage affects build approach, integration count, partner sequencing, architecture, ownership boundaries, acceptance logic, or commercial assumptions, that item shall remain governed as an unresolved dependency and shall not be treated as implicitly approved.

The realization and testing milestone(s) shall cover the approved delivery scope required to prepare the solution for deployment. These milestone(s) shall include configuration, approved delta development, integration realization, test preparation, test execution support, defect governance, training preparation, and release-readiness activities for the approved phase baseline. Internal sprint completion alone shall not constitute milestone completion unless the resulting outputs satisfy the applicable acceptance framework and review requirements.

The deployment milestone shall apply to the approved release baseline for production transition. This milestone shall only be considered achieved when the agreed cutover activities are completed, required production-validation checks have been performed, open critical issues have been dispositioned in accordance with the agreed release controls, and Google has issued written confirmation for the approved release scope.

The Hypercare and transition milestone shall confirm completion of the agreed stabilization and handoff activities for the approved release. This milestone is limited to the agreed hypercare support period and transition scope defined elsewhere in this SOW. It shall not be interpreted as creating any ongoing managed-services, production-support, or post-hypercare support obligation unless such scope is expressly approved in this SOW or a later written amendment.

The milestone structure in this section shall also govern how delivery readiness is reviewed across the engagement. Before any major phase, release, or go-live event is treated as ready to proceed, the applicable governance forum shall review, at a minimum:

- completion status of approved deliverables for that milestone;
- status of key assumptions, issues, risks, dependencies, and deferred decisions;
- interface, environment, and access readiness for the affected scope;
- data readiness and testing readiness for the affected release;
- training, change, and business-readiness status where applicable;
- unresolved defects, open actions, and release-impacting exceptions;
- whether any open item requires formal change control before progression.

Where any such decision changes the approved baseline, the impact shall be evaluated for scope, effort, timeline, testing, deployment, and commercials, and shall be managed through the Change Management Process in Section 17 before the affected work is committed or executed as contracted scope.

In addition to milestone governance, this section establishes the treatment of deferred scope decisions. The parties acknowledge that several design and operating-model decisions remain open as of this draft and may materially affect phase content, delivery sequencing, technical realization, and commercial assumptions. These deferred items shall not be treated as approved by implication because related planning, design, or dependency work has begun. Each deferred item shall be logged with an owner, target resolution date, impacted phase, and dependency effect.

If a deferred decision is not resolved in time to support the planned milestone sequence, the parties shall either:

- approve a documented interim operating approach with identified owners, controls, business impact, and retirement criteria; or
- defer the affected capability, partner, integration, geography, deliverable, or release content to a later approved phase or formal change.

This section also establishes safeguards for integration growth and custom-code growth. The approved integration and technical baseline for this engagement is limited to the interfaces, data exchanges, and approved delta enablement expressly identified in this SOW. Any addition of a new interface, source system, target system, message type, partner-specific format, downstream consumer, report, dashboard, custom object, enhancement, workflow, reconciliation utility, or related technical item not expressly included in the approved baseline shall be treated as out of scope unless and until it is formally approved through Section 17.

To maintain control over technical scope, the following safeguards shall apply:

- The approved interface inventory and approved custom-object inventory shall be confirmed and frozen before dependent build proceeds for each phase.
- Reuse of existing approved frameworks, templates, and integration assets is expected where feasible; however, if such reuse proves insufficient and net-new work is required, the impact shall be formally assessed before inclusion.
- Any increase in integration count, message variants, data feeds, consuming systems, partner-specific connectivity, or custom technical objects shall be treated as a scope-impacting event.
- No technical object or interface shall proceed into build, test, or deployment until its business purpose, dependency set, owner, and acceptance path are sufficiently documented for the affected phase.
- Any request for additional reports, integrations, automations, partner-specific changes, or technical variants raised after baseline approval shall be evaluated through formal governance and, where material, through the Change Management Process in Section 17.
- Any interim manual process adopted because an integration, automation, or custom object is not yet approved or available shall be documented with owner, control points, business impact, and retirement criteria before use.

The parties further agree that no workstream shall absorb scope growth informally. This applies equally to growth in integrations, data sources, message standards, partner onboarding, reports, analytics, deployment scope, training scope, or technical development. Any such increase shall be assessed for schedule, effort, testing, acceptance, deployment, and commercial impact before it is incorporated into the delivery baseline.

Risk management under this section shall be active and governance-driven. The approved Risks section elsewhere in this SOW identifies the principal risk themes currently known for this engagement, including deferred decisions, integration and custom-code growth, stakeholder availability, acceptance ambiguity, BOM ownership, Kinaxis environment strategy, partner-operating-model uncertainty, source-system readiness, data quality, regression impact, misunderstanding of excluded scope, and post-go-live stabilization risk. These risks shall be tracked through the agreed governance structure and reflected in the applicable risk logs, status reporting, and milestone-readiness reviews.

As a minimum governance requirement for risk mitigation:

- each material risk shall have a named owner, mitigation action, and target review cadence;
- risks affecting milestone readiness shall be raised before the affected milestone is treated as committed;
- risks tied to client decisions, partner readiness, or technical dependencies shall be escalated early through the program-governance forum;
- any risk event that changes scope, timing, cost, or delivery responsibility shall be evaluated for formal change-control treatment;
- any risk accepted for interim continuation shall be explicitly recorded with business impact and approving authority.

This section also confirms that any change affecting approved scope, partner coverage, technical boundary, milestone timing, deliverables, assumptions, exclusions, testing baseline, cutover approach, hypercare scope, or commercials shall be managed through the formal Change Management Process in Section 17. No workshop output, sprint discussion, design note, testing observation, or governance conversation shall by itself modify the contracted baseline.

Accordingly, pending formal approval under Section 17:

- Bristlecone shall have no obligation to perform work outside the approved baseline;
- Google shall have no obligation to accept or pay for work not formally approved as part of the SOW baseline;
- future-phase items, exploratory options, and deferred decisions shall not be treated as committed delivery scope;
- excluded and client-owned activities shall remain excluded or client-owned unless expressly added through approved change.

This section is intended to ensure that milestone execution, deferred decisions, technical scope growth, and delivery risk are controlled in a disciplined manner across the life of the engagement. Any more detailed milestone mapping, release-governance detail, or working-level tracking structure developed during project initiation or execution must remain consistent with the approved scope, deliverables, acceptance criteria, exclusions, assumptions, and commercials stated in this SOW.

This Appendix summarizes the indicative Bristlecone resource profile expectations for the approved scope of this SOW and should be read together with Section 7.2 (Roles & Responsibilities), Section 8 (Personnel Requirements), Section 13.2 (Rate Card & Pyramid Structure), and the approved phase structure elsewhere in this document. It is intended to describe the expected qualifications, domain background, and certification profile for key delivery roles supporting the engagement across Explore, Build, Deploy, and Hypercare.

Because this SOW remains a draft and several staffing, location, and commercial items remain subject to confirmation, this Appendix defines the expected role profile baseline and minimum qualification direction for the engagement rather than naming individual personnel. Any client approval rights, named-person commitments, replacement rules, or mandatory staffing constraints remain subject to the governing agreement and related confirmed staffing approvals.

The delivery team is expected to include a cross-functional mix of program, architecture, functional, technical, integration, data, testing, deployment, and organizational change resources capable of supporting the approved scope across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, E2Open Vendor Collaboration, Silicon Data Hub, G-Plan, GPLM, and related approved handoffs. Consistent with the approved roles and responsibilities structure, the resource model is expected to support coordination across onsite and offshore delivery, with final role-wise deployment locations, staffing counts, and ramp timing subject to confirmation through the approved staffing plan.

At a minimum, Bristlecone personnel assigned to this engagement should collectively provide the following profile coverage:

- program and project governance leadership for a multi-phase enterprise transformation;
- solution architecture capability spanning planning, execution, collaboration, integration, and traceability layers;
- SAP S/4HANA functional and technical capability aligned to the approved PP/MM-centered silicon manufacturing and subcontracting scope;
- Kinaxis planning design and configuration capability aligned to the approved supply planning, inventory planning, and constraint-planning scope;
- integration and data capability across approved enterprise, planning, partner-collaboration, and genealogy-related interfaces;
- testing, cutover, and hypercare capability for multi-system release execution;
- organizational change management and training capability aligned to the approved persona-based adoption approach.

The delivery team should also demonstrate prior experience working in complex supply chain, semiconductor, high-tech manufacturing, or similarly traceability-intensive environments, particularly where planning decisions depend on external manufacturing visibility, subcontracting control, supplier collaboration, lot genealogy, and yield-aware planning inputs.

The following role-profile expectations apply for the principal Bristlecone delivery roles under this SOW:

- **Program Sponsor**
 - Senior leadership experience overseeing large, cross-functional enterprise transformation or implementation programs.
 - Experience governing complex client programs with multiple workstreams, milestone dependencies, escalation management, and executive steering participation.
 - Ability to provide strategic oversight, resource alignment, risk escalation support, and executive-level commercial and delivery governance.
 - Typical qualification expectation: `<CONFIRM: minimum years of experience for Program Sponsor>`.
 - Recommended certifications may include recognized program or delivery-governance credentials, where applicable, such as `<CONFIRM: whether any formal program-governance certification is required>`.

- **Program Manager / Project Manager / PMO**
 - Demonstrated experience leading phased enterprise implementations across design, build, testing, deployment, and stabilization.
 - Strong capability in integrated planning, RAID management, milestone control, governance reporting, dependency management, and release-readiness coordination.
 - Experience coordinating multi-application and cross-functional delivery teams, including onsite and offshore work models.
 - Familiarity with agile and hybrid delivery methods, sprint planning, issue triage, and phase-gate controls.
 - Typical qualification expectation: `<CONFIRM: minimum years of experience for Program Manager / PMO roles>`.
 - Recommended certifications may include PMP, PRINCE2, Scrum Master, or equivalent, subject to `<CONFIRM: whether project-management certifications are mandatory>`.

- **Solution Architect**
 - Experience designing end-to-end enterprise solutions across planning, execution, collaboration, integration, and data platforms.
 - Ability to align process design, system boundaries, integration patterns, data ownership, non-functional considerations, and phased rollout strategy.
 - Prior experience in supply chain, manufacturing, semiconductor, or high-tech planning architectures is strongly preferred.
 - Ability to govern architecture decisions across SAP S/4HANA, Kinaxis, partner-collaboration layers, data platforms, and integration components within the approved scope.
 - Typical qualification expectation: `<CONFIRM: minimum years of experience for Solution Architect>`.
 - Recommended certifications may include architecture or platform credentials relevant to the approved system landscape, subject to `<CONFIRM: whether specific architecture certifications are required>`.

 - Experience in SAP S/4HANA process design and configuration for the approved PP/MM-centered scope.
 - Familiarity with procurement, subcontracting, material master, BOM structures, routing support, goods movement, inventory visibility, and traceability-supporting process enablement.
 - Experience supporting functional specifications, user stories, testing, cutover support, and business-process validation in enterprise implementations.
 - Semiconductor or similar manufacturing-domain experience is strongly preferred where role scope includes foundry or OSAT operating-model support.
 - Typical qualification expectation: `<CONFIRM: minimum years of experience for SAP S/4HANA Functional Lead and Consultant roles>`.
 - Recommended certifications may include current SAP certifications aligned to the approved process scope, subject to `<CONFIRM: whether SAP certification is mandatory for lead and/or consultant roles>`.

 - Recommended certifications may include relevant SAP technical certifications, subject to `<CONFIRM: whether SAP technical certifications are mandatory>`.

 - Ability to work within the approved boundary that Bristlecone supports planning business rules and functionality for the in-scope planning landscape, while final ownership for certain external integration build responsibilities remains subject to confirmation.

 - Typical qualification expectation: `<CONFIRM: minimum years of experience for E2Open / Partner Collaboration Lead>`.

 - Recommended certifications may include ISTQB or equivalent testing credentials, subject to `<CONFIRM: whether formal testing certifications are mandatory>`.

 - Experience supporting stakeholder assessment, change-impact analysis, communications planning, training development, persona-based adoption support, readiness assessments, and knowledge transfer.
